description: Somos un equipo de tres estudiantes universitarios de distintas disciplinas unidos por nuestro interés en la ciencia, tecnología y exploración espacial. Participamos del NASA Space Apps Challenge para desarrollar una propuesta innovadora sobre la supervivencia humana en Marte. Nos interesan las ciencias planetarias, la exploración espacial y tecnología aplicadas a misiones. Buscamos incorporar participantes con conocimientos en programación, IA y análisis de datos que aporten nuevas perspectivas
summary:
MARSBOARD is a web-based Mars exploration console developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. It provides an interactive map of the AP-1 candidate landing site (Arcadia/Amazonis Planitia) with NASA data layers including topography, geophysics, and optical imagery. Users can explore points of interest, plan surface routes between stations, and receive warnings about hazardous terrain segments. The tool features a mission-control-style HUD interface, requires no registration, and includes local fallback data so it remains functional during live demos.

By translating open NASA planetary data into an intuitive visual interface, MARSBOARD helps mission planners and the public quickly identify safe sites, traverse routes, and understand operational needs on Mars. It addresses the challenge of making complex space mission data accessible within short evaluation windows, supporting human exploration by highlighting where and how crews can operate on the Martian surface.
details:
What does the project do and how does it work?

MARSBOARD is a web console for exploring Mars. It shows an interactive map of the AP-1 region (Arcadia/Amazonis Planitia) with NASA data layers (topography, geophysics, optical images). It traces routes between stations and warns if a section of terrain could be dangerous.

What benefits does it have?

- Helps quickly understand where points of interest on Mars are located.

- Easy to use: judges and visitors can explore it in seconds without registration.

- Generates reports ready to print or copy.

- Works even if the connection to NASA data fails, because it has a local backup version.

What is the expected impact?

Support human exploration of Mars by providing a simple visual tool to plan missions: choose safe sites, view routes, and understand what is needed to operate on the surface. It also makes NASA open data accessible to the general public.

What tools, languages, hardware or software did you use?

- Frontend: Next.js, React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Leaflet (maps).

- Backend: Node.js, Express.

- Data: NASA map layers (Mars Trek, MOLA, CTX, HiRISE, among others).

- Deployment: Docker and Nginx.

- Version control: Git and GitHub.

How is the project creative?

- It has a "mission console" aesthetic (dark theme, HUD-style colors, map ping animations).

- It does not show overwhelming raw data: it prioritizes that someone understands the purpose in less than 30 seconds.

What factors did the team consider?

- Judges have little time to evaluate, so the interface is clear and direct.

- Focus on a single Mars site (AP-1) and do it well, instead of covering the whole planet superficially.
